Tectonic Summary
The January 26, 2001, M 7.7 earthquake near Gujarat, India, occurred as the result of shallow oblique reverse faulting within the continental crust of the India plate, near the India-Eurasia plate boundary where there is both transform and convergent motion. Focal mechanism solutions for the earthquake indicate that oblique rupture occurred on either an east-northeast-, or a west-northwest-striking, moderately dipping reverse fault. Of these two possible fault orientations, finite-fault modeling of globally recorded seismic data is more consistent with slip on the east-northeast-striking fault. At the location of this earthquake, the India plate moves northward with respect to the Eurasia plate at a velocity of about 39 mm/yr.
